approachQuestion.prompt:
An array lists switches, each represented by an unsigned W-bit word. Choose any subset, possibly empty, and XOR its words. Return the largest unsigned value obtainable. Each switch may be selected at most once.

Constraints: 1 <= W <= 64; W <= n <= 200000. Return only the maximum word.
Example: W=4, [3,5,6,0] -> 6. The available results are 0,3,5,6. Edge case: W=1, [0] -> 0.

Choose the best approach under these constraints.
constraints: W is a parameter; a W-bit XOR, bit test or unsigned comparison is one word operation. Allocate a W-entry pivot array. No arbitrary-precision arithmetic is needed.
Inputs are read-only. Include all temporary storage and any call stack; exclude the supplied input and the returned output. No input copy is implicit.

options.text: Reduce each input from high bit to low against existing pivot words; store the first missing pivot. Then visit pivots high to low, XORing one into the answer exactly when it increases the answer.
options.feedback: Pivot reduction preserves the span of all subset XORs. High-to-low maximization chooses each leading bit without sacrificing earlier decisions.

options.text: Enumerate every subset, compute its XOR, and return the maximum.
options.feedback: This is correct but explicitly inefficient: independent switches can create exponentially many subsets, while only W pivot positions are needed.

options.text: Select every switch and return their total XOR.
options.feedback: Selecting all need not maximize the result. For W=2 and [1,2,3], total XOR is 0 but choosing 3 gives 3.

options.text: Return the largest value among individual words and XORs of pairs, also considering zero.
options.feedback: For W=3 and [1,2,4], every pair is at most 6, but all three produce 7.

feedback.reason: An independent leading pivot expands the representable XOR space; a dependent word reduces to zero and adds no new combinations.
details: Maintain at most one basis word per leading set-bit position. Eliminate existing leading pivots from each incoming word; retain a new independent pivot when needed. Starting from zero, consider pivots from the highest position downward and apply each if it increases the unsigned result.

An independent leading pivot expands the representable XOR space; a dependent word reduces to zero and adds no new combinations. Greedily improving from high pivots finds the largest unsigned subset XOR, including the empty subset zero.

“Reduce each input from high bit to low against existing pivot words; store the first missing pivot. Then visit pivots high to low, XORing one into the answer exactly when it increases the answer.”: Pivot reduction preserves the span of all subset XORs. High-to-low maximization chooses each leading bit without sacrificing earlier decisions.

“Enumerate every subset, compute its XOR, and return the maximum.”: This is correct but explicitly inefficient: independent switches can create exponentially many subsets, while only W pivot positions are needed.
“Select every switch and return their total XOR.”: Selecting all need not maximize the result. For W=2 and [1,2,3], total XOR is 0 but choosing 3 gives 3.
“Return the largest value among individual words and XORs of pairs, also considering zero.”: For W=3 and [1,2,4], every pair is at most 6, but all three produce 7.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For build-xor-basis, choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. Let n be the array length and W the bit width.
constraints: W is a parameter; a W-bit XOR, bit test or unsigned comparison is one word operation. Allocate a W-entry pivot array. No arbitrary-precision arithmetic is needed.
Inputs are read-only. Include all temporary storage and any call stack; exclude the supplied input and the returned output. No input copy is implicit.

feedback.reason: Examine up to W pivot positions per value and retain W basis words.
details: Every input can require examining W pivot positions, including dependent words reducing to zero. There are W stored pivots and no recursion or subset list.
W is a parameter; a W-bit XOR, bit test or unsigned comparison is one word operation. Allocate a W-entry pivot array. No arbitrary-precision arithmetic is needed.
“O(nW) time, O(nW) auxiliary space”: Only W pivots are retained, regardless of n.
“O(2^n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: That describes subset enumeration, not elimination.
“O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: Reduction may test all W positions and stores a width-sized basis.
